mainEntity.name: What is the best backup plan if my AI demo fails during the webinar?

acceptedAnswer.text: Prepare a backup plan that covers the deck, speaker notes, demonstration, presenter connection, audience communication, and recording. Keep a downloadable version of the slides, a non-live example, a second presenter or moderator where possible, and a way to notify attendees if the session changes. Context: AI demonstrations add dependency on platforms, accounts, permissions, integrations, and internet access. Key factors: - Which parts require live software - Availability of a recording or screenshots - Moderator communication - Attendee expectations Practical guidance: Rehearse the fallback as part of the technical test. If a live tool fails, explain the intended workflow with prepared screenshots rather than improvising account access. Never expose private credentials, participant data, or unreviewed generated output while troubleshooting.
acceptedAnswer.description: Keep a reviewed slide or video version of the demonstration, downloadable speaker notes, screenshots of key steps, and a moderator communication plan. Rehearse the fallback, avoid exposing credentials or participant data, and explain the intended workflow clearly instead of improvising access to live accounts.
